title: Verifier‑Augmented vs. LLM‑Only NetOps Agents: A Paired Evaluation on an Action‑Aware Staging Benchmark
abstract: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact‑backed paired evaluation comparing a verifier‑augmented NetOps pipeline to an LLM‑only pipeline on ActionAwareStagingBench‑v1. The preregistered design employed gpt‑5‑mini as the generator, deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as runtime guard and post‑hoc scorer, N=400 paired tasks (800 episodes), and shared_initial_generation semantics (one shared LLM candidate per task delivered to both conditions). Confirmatory outcomes (from archived analysis artifacts) are exact and deterministic: complete_pairs = 400; baseline_success_count = 400/400; guarded_success_count = 400/400; paired contingency n_11 = 400, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0; observed paired difference = 0.0; preregistered permutation p = 1.0; exact McNemar p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap_seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples). Diagnostics using execution and reconciliation artifacts show that shared_initial_generation together with reuse of the same deterministic validator created a deterministic ceiling that made the primary estimand uninformative in this run. We present the preregistered methodology, exact artifact‑grounded results, an operational diagnosis of the ceiling mechanism supported by provider_call_audit and validator traces, and concrete artifact‑grounded recommendations to harden future benchmarks so they expose generator×guard interactions.

sections.introduction:
Large language models (LLMs) are being proposed to translate operator intent into network configuration artifacts and staged change workflows (canaries, progressive rollout, rollback). Prior work demonstrates that LLMs can produce syntactically plausible configuration templates in controlled datasets and testbeds, and separate lines of research show verifier‑guided generate–validate–repair loops and deterministic network verifiers reduce syntactic and semantic errors in infrastructure‑as‑code and related domains. The operational safety question motivating this study is end‑to‑end: how do generator variability, runtime verification, staged rollout semantics, repair, and rollback interact to determine safe‑deploy outcomes in agentic NetOps pipelines?

Research question. Under the ActionAwareStagingBench‑v1 semantics used here, does integrating a deterministic runtime validator with an LLM generator increase paired safe‑deploy rate relative to an LLM‑only pipeline? The preregistered primary estimand was the paired difference in safe‑deploy rate (guarded − baseline) measured on N=400 preregistered paired tasks using a paired‑binary confirmatory design.

Summary of contributions. (1) A fully preregistered paired evaluation executed with gpt‑5‑mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; every runtime trace, validator trace, and analysis artifact was archived. (2) Artifact‑grounded confirmatory result: a deterministic ceiling—both conditions achieved 100% safe‑deploy across 400 pairs (paired difference = 0.0; permutation p = 1.0). (3) A diagnostic, evidence‑grounded explanation of why the design produced a ceiling (shared_initial_generation + single deterministic validator used both at runtime and for scoring) and a concrete set of preregisterable hardening recommendations (independent per‑condition generation, distinct post‑hoc scorer, controlled adversarial seeding, difficulty‑stratified sampling, and instrumented mitigation metrics) that are implementable using the archived task manifest and validator traces.
sections.related_work: Three intersecting literatures motivate the experiment and the hardening recommendations. First, intent→configuration generation: recent efforts (prototype systems and datasets) show LLMs can map natural‑language intent to configuration artifacts but evaluation is often on curated corpora or testbeds rather than live networks. Representative works include intent‑to‑configuration demonstrations and pretrained/fine‑tuning efforts for configuration generation; these establish feasibility but highlight dataset and generalization gaps. Second, verifier‑guided workflows and deterministic verification: studies in IaC and provisioning (verifier‑guided fine‑tuning, verifier‑in‑the‑loop systems) and deterministic network verifiers demonstrate that strong verifiers can catch many classes of errors offline; however, closed‑loop runtime integration and the joint generator×verifier dynamics are less explored. Third, agentic/tool‑augmented architectures (ReAct, RAG, multi‑agent orchestrations) broaden capabilities for AIOps but introduce failure modes—hallucination, misapplied tools, and overconfident outputs—that motivate runtime guardrails and staged deployments. Surveys and evaluation‑gap reviews repeatedly call for action‑aware benchmarks combining generation, runtime blocking, staged rollout, repair, rollback, and provenance; our study operationalizes such a compact benchmark and shows a concrete pitfall for paired evaluations when design choices collapse the statistical signal.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimands. The study preregistration (cnsmauto‑3d2k‑prereg‑v1) specified a paired binary design with exactly N=400 paired tasks, primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, and a permutation‑based paired difference test as the primary confirmatory procedure. An exact McNemar two‑sided test and paired bootstrap CIs were prespecified for corroboration. Secondary prespecified outcomes included bootstrap CIs for median time‑to‑rollback and counts of repair attempts.

Execution contract and critical design choices. Execution used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter family with declared generator gpt‑5‑mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as both runtime guard and post‑hoc scorer. The preregistration set shared_initial_generation = true (independent_condition_generation = false): for each task we obtained one LLM candidate and delivered that identical candidate to both baseline and guarded episodes. This choice intentionally isolated the validator’s acceptance decision on identical generator outputs and reduced model‑call budget (model_calls_used = 400 for 800 episodes; maximum_model_calls = 800). The adapter permitted up to one repair call in the guarded episode; repair traces and repair_applied flags were recorded (repair_applied = false across episodes).

Task generation, replay, and scoring. Tasks were produced by a seed‑controlled deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 yielding structured difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, pattern, required_command_count, level ∈ {medium, hard, very_hard}). Deterministic replay checks were applied and passed for all pairs. Scoring was performed by deterministic_netops_validator_v5 using full intent‑constraint validation; validator traces record validation_before/after, final_configuration, repair_applied, and validity decisions. All execution and analysis artifacts supporting measurements were archived and used without manual adjudication.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The run started 2026‑08‑29T18:23:37Z and completed 2026‑08‑29T19:12:38Z. Planned episodes = 800; completed episodes = 800; failed episodes = 0; model_calls_used = 400 (shared initial generation). Deterministic replay checks passed for all pairs; no exclusions were recorded.

Confirmatory outcomes (artifact‑grounded). From the archived confirmatory analysis: complete_pairs = 400; baseline_success_count = 400 (baseline_success_rate = 1.0); guarded_success_count = 400 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n_11 = 400 with n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0, yielding observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. The preregistered permutation test returned p = 1.0; the exact McNemar two‑sided test returned p = 1.0. The paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap_seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples). Cohen's h = 0.0. These numeric values are reproduced directly from the archived analysis outputs.

Repair, rollback, and difficulty aggregation. Across all 800 episodes repair_applied = false and no rollbacks were invoked; validator traces show validation_after.final_state matched expected_final_state for accepted configurations. The archived task manifest yields the following difficulty distribution: medium: 80 tasks (20.0%); hard: 160 tasks (40.0%); very_hard: 160 tasks (40.0%)—these counts were extracted verbatim from the task manifest. Provider and reconciliation diagnostics. The deterministic_reconciliation artifact records provider_call_audit: hosted_model_call_event_count = 400, cache_miss_count = 400, stage_counts: {shared_initial_generation: 400}, condition_counts: {shared: 400}, and all deterministic consistency checks passed. These records empirically document the shared generation semantics and an absence of cross‑condition model call variation.
sections.discussion:
Why the design produced a deterministic ceiling. Two preregistered choices created the observed ceiling. First, shared_initial_generation removed generator variance by delivering identical LLM outputs to baseline and guarded episodes. Second, the runtime guard and post‑hoc scorer were the same deterministic implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). When the deterministic validator accepts the shared candidate, both conditions necessarily record safe‑deploy outcomes and the paired difference is forced to zero. This is a construct‑validity outcome of the frozen design; it does not imply that verifiers lack utility under other generation/verification pairings.

Interpretation for confirmatory inference and power. The confirmatory tests (permutation, exact McNemar) correctly report p = 1.0 given the data, and the paired bootstrap CI correctly collapses to a point mass at zero. However, these inferential outputs have no practical information about generator×guard closed‑loop dynamics because the design prevented the guard from having an opportunity to intervene. The preregistered power rationale assumed non‑ceiling baseline failure rates; that assumption was falsified by the frozen generator+validator pairing and thus does not apply here.

Operational implications and concrete hardening recommendations. To preserve opportunities for runtime guards to accept, block, or request repair, researchers should preregister designs that do not conflate generator variance and scorer invariance. Artifact‑grounded, implementable recommendations supported by the archived manifests and traces are: (1) independent per‑condition generation (independent_condition_generation = true) so each condition draws its own LLM candidate; (2) use a distinct post‑hoc scorer or held‑out adjudicator (different implementation or a validator with stochastic perturbation) to avoid conflating runtime blocking and measurement; (3) controlled adversarial seeding to guarantee nontrivial baseline failure rates (seeded tasks that the generator is likely to fail without verifier intervention); (4) difficulty‑stratified sampling to ensure sufficient representation of very_hard tasks (the archived manifest contains per‑task difficulty labels enabling deterministic stratified resampling); and (5) instrumented mitigation metrics (repair_attempts, repairs_applied, time‑to‑rollback) recorded as explicit numeric outcomes. Each recommendation is directly actionable using artifacts in the archive (task manifest difficulty labels, validator traces that already contain repair_applied and validation timestamps, and provider_call_audit logs).

Threats to validity and limitations. Internal validity is reduced here by shared generation and reuse of the same validator for runtime and scoring. Construct validity: the deterministic validator approximates production checks but does not model telemetry noise, asynchronous states, or stochastic adjudication policies. External validity is limited by use of a single generator (gpt‑5‑mini) and a single deterministic validator; results do not generalize across models, validators, or production heterogeneity. Adversarial robustness was not exercised and remains an open empirical question. The detailed limitations list is reported separately.
sections.conclusion:
We executed a fully preregistered paired evaluation comparing a verifier‑augmented NetOps pipeline to an LLM‑only pipeline under ActionAwareStagingBench‑v1. Under the preregistered shared_initial_generation semantics and the chosen generator+validator pairing, every shared candidate satisfied deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and both conditions produced 100% safe‑deploy across N=400 pairs (paired difference = 0.0; permutation p = 1.0). The resulting deterministic ceiling is a design artifact caused by identical per‑pair generation and reuse of a deterministic validator for runtime blocking and post‑hoc scoring; it renders the primary estimand uninformative for generator×guard closed‑loop interactions in this run. We archive the preregistration and full execution/analysis artifacts to enable reproducibility. The artifact‑grounded hardening recommendations supplied here (independent generation per condition, distinct scorer, controlled adversarial seeding, difficulty stratification, and mitigation metrics) provide concrete steps to preserve statistical signal when evaluating runtime verifier utility in NetOps settings. Future runs that implement these hardening steps—possible using the archived task manifest and validator traces—can exercise blocking, repair, and rollback behaviors meaningfully and restore inferential relevance for the primary estimand.

Reproducibility. All execution and analysis artifacts supporting reported numbers and traces are archived in the bundled artifact set and include the execution manifest, raw results, model configuration, deterministic validator traces, task manifest with per‑task difficulty metadata, and analysis results (paired contingency and bootstrap outputs). The deterministic reconciliation and provider_call_audit artifacts document shared_initial_generation and the model call accounting used in the confirmatory analysis. Auditors can reproduce the reported summaries using the archived manifests and analysis code recorded in the artifact bundle.

Disclosure Statement (mandatory). Declared generator: gpt‑5‑mini. Orchestration: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter family with shared_initial_generation semantics (independent_condition_generation = false) as preregistered. Runtime guard and post‑hoc scorer: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Preregistration: cnsmauto‑3d2k‑prereg‑v1. The immutable initial master prompt is archived as provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. The guarded condition routed the shared LLM candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 which deterministically accepted or blocked candidates per the preregistered adapter policy; the adapter allowed up to one repair call per task but none were applied (repair_applied = false). All runtime calls, raw outputs, validator traces, deterministic replay checks, exclusion logs, and analysis artifacts are archived in the artifact bundle and were used without manual adjudication.

Limitations: [1] Benchmark hardness and ceiling effect: under preregistered shared_initial_generation semantics and the chosen generator+validator, every shared candidate satisfied deterministic_netops_validator_v5 so the guard had no opportunity to alter outcomes; this makes the primary estimand effectively untestable in this run and invalidates the original power rationale. [2] Model and scope: the experiment used a single generator (gpt‑5‑mini) and a single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); results do not generalize across models, validators, or production heterogeneity. [3] Construct validity: the same deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementation served as both runtime guard and the post‑hoc scorer; this conflation produces concordant acceptance/scoring and limits inference about independent closed‑loop verifier utility. [4] Shared candidate semantics: preregistered shared_initial_generation intentionally reduces generation variance and therefore limits inference to the validator’s behavior on identical candidates rather than full generator+guard closed‑loop interactions. [5] Synthetic environment and external validity: the simulator and validator do not fully model production telemetry noise, operator workflows, or adversarial actor behaviours; external validity to live networks is limited. [6] Adversarial robustness untested: adversarial or distribution‑shifted prompts and generator faults that could trigger guard interventions were not exercised in this run and remain open for future work. [7] Aggregated difficulty reporting: the full per‑task difficulty labels for all N=400 are archived in the task manifest and can be reaggregated by auditors; Table 1 reports the artifact‑extracted aggregated counts and percentages.
